commander: Friedrich August Freiherr von der Heydte
current_activity: about one hundred scattered paratroopers reach the rendezvous on the Eupen road north of Mont Rigi
notes: Event date: 17 December 1944, after the night drop (Cole, ch. 11). Event definition: After a scattered night drop, about one hundred paratroopers reach the rendezvous at the fork in the Eupen road north of Mont Rigi, where Heydte forms a camp in the woods; Wikipedia places the position at Porfays (Cole, ch. 11; Wikipedia, Operation Stösser). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 11, p. 271: "about one hundred paratroopers reached the rendezvous at the fork in the Eupen road north of Mont Rigi"; Wikipedia, Operation Stösser: "Kampfgruppe Von Der Heydte took up a position at Porfays". Location: Porfays, Eupen road north of Mont Rigi (new place, approximate) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Cole names the fork north of Mont Rigi; Wikipedia names Porfays. Commander: Colonel Friedrich August Freiherr von der Heydte (Cole, ch. 11).

commander: Friedrich August Freiherr von der Heydte
current_activity: Heydte, wounded, surrenders at Monschau after the battle group disperses
notes: Event date: 23 December 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: Heydte reaches Monschau on 21 December and surrenders on 23 December (Wikipedia, Operation Stösser and Friedrich August Freiherr von der Heydte). Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, Friedrich August Freiherr von der Heydte: "Heydte arrived in Monschau on 21 December and surrendered on 23 December". Location: Monschau with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Monschau. Commander: Colonel Friedrich August Freiherr von der Heydte (Cole, ch. 11).
